title: Getting ready for AI: Executive Director Nicolas Vasse at ESMA Data Day 2026

paras.text: Vasse underlined that AI offers supervisors significant opportunities, from analysing large volumes of data and detecting emerging ML/TF risks to making supervisory work more efficient. Looking ahead, he noted that the technology is evolving rapidly and that supervisors will need to keep adapting their tools and processes.

He outlined how AMLA is preparing to make the most of data and AI in its supervisory work. The Authority is building its own infrastructure and data platform, formalising its supervisory processes and setting up its data collection so that AI can add value from the outset. He described the implementation of AI as an ongoing research and development effort, with people remaining at the centre of key decisions.

In line with the "report once, use many times" principle, AMLA is working with the European Central Bank, the European Supervisory Authorities and national authorities to use existing data and develop common data definitions, so that future data collections avoid duplicate efforts. Given the sensitivity of AML/CFT work, AMLA's approach also combines access to the latest innovation with strong standards of security and data protection.
He concluded that there is no ready-made recipe for AI, and that agility, cooperation and continuous learning across the supervisory community will be essential to make the most of new technologies.
